title: Shipyard workflow worker return
description: Structured result a /shipyard:do-work worker returns. Every `mode:`-driven worker (issue-work, fix-checks-only, fix-rebase, fix-main-ci, fix-failing-prs-batch, investigate, spike) is dispatched through the `Agent` tool with isolation: "worktree" and returns this shape as its terminal string. This schema is the canonical, reviewable definition of that return vocabulary — see skills/worker-preamble/SKILL.md § "Return-contract discipline" for how a worker renders it, and hand it to an `Agent`/`Workflow` `schema` option to have the harness validate a stage result mechanically instead of parsing the terminal string.

mode.description: The worker mode this result came from — the same value the dispatch prompt names as `mode:` (agents/issue-worker.md routing table). Lets the orchestrator's reconcile validate that the structured result's shape matches the mode it dispatched.

outcome.description: Terminal outcome class, mapping onto the free-text return-string leading token. `awaiting-external` — the worker did everything it could and the only remaining input is a long external job (a dispatched CI run, an EAS/store build, a deploy) reaching a terminal state; TERMINAL and NOT a human hand-back — no `needs-human-review`, no `blocked:ci` cap increment, no `/my-turn` surfacing (#1390). Requires `awaiting_what` + `awaiting_probe`; the orchestrator records them in its `awaiting_external` queue, re-runs the probe each refresh tick, and resumes the SAME agent when it goes terminal. Modelled on `pending` (below), generalized from a PR's own rollup to an arbitrary external job. `shipped` — issue-work opened a PR (see auto_merge). `green` — fix-checks-only drove an existing PR's checks green (checks must be "green" with an evidence-clause summary — see #985/#987). `pending` — fix-checks-only found nothing failing but the rollup hasn't fully settled (checks:"pending"); an honest, non-overclaiming exit distinct from `green` — does not count toward the 3-attempt cap, no `blocked:ci` label (#985/#987). `dirty` — fix-checks-only found the PR's `mergeStateStatus` is DIRTY (conflicts with the default branch) before any checks could queue at all — GitHub can't compute a merge ref, so `pull_request`-triggered workflows never run; not a CI failure, so it does not count toward the 3-attempt cap and does not earn `blocked:ci` — the orchestrator routes it to the drain's `fix-rebase` path instead (#1015). `rebased` — fix-rebase rebased a DIRTY PR onto the default branch. `noop` — a fix mode found nothing to do (e.g. the failing run resolved itself between dispatch and read). `blocked` — a real blocker was hit before completion (see blocked_reason); the orchestrator's step-A reconcile classifies it into needs-human-review / blocked:agent-soft / no-label per #521. `reaped` — the worktree was reaped mid-run; RETRYABLE, re-enqueued with no block label (distinct from `blocked`). `disposition` — investigate/spike mode dispositioned the issue without a PR (see disposition).

issue.description: The issue number this dispatch targeted (#N). Null for synthetic diverts with no originating issue (fix-main-ci, fix-failing-prs-batch).

pr.description: The PR number this dispatch opened or acted on (#M). Present on `shipped` / `green` / `pending` / `dirty` / `rebased`; null on `noop` / `blocked` / `reaped` / a no-PR `disposition`.

incidental_pr.description: Optional. For a `disposition: "verified"` outcome only (issue-work §6.6, the QA-verification carve-out): the PR number of a small, non-closing incidental test-coverage fix opened via issue-work-verification-dispatch.md's narrow step-3 exception (#1044) — a `Refs #<N>` reference, never a closing keyword, so it has no bearing on the verified issue's own disposition. Distinct from `pr`, which stays null on this outcome (there is still no *resolving* PR for the dispatched issue). Unlike the null-`pr` case, a non-null `incidental_pr` IS appended to `session_prs` by the orchestrator's reconcile — it's a real PR with its own checks/merge lifecycle. Null when no such PR was opened (the common case).

auto_merge.description: For `shipped` (issue-work), the auto-merge outcome — the structured form of the return-string `(auto-merge: …)` suffix. `enabled`: --auto armed, queued behind checks. `gated-manual`: the ungated-admin-direct-merge pre-check (#598/#716) fired, worker watched checks and merged by hand. `merged-direct`: --auto fell through to an immediate merge with checks green at merge time. `merged-direct-ungated`: same, but the PR landed before CI completed (no required checks — #457). `unavailable`: the merge call genuinely failed for a generic/transient/repo-config reason, needs manual merge. `unavailable-workflow-scope`: the merge call failed specifically because the gh token lacks the `workflow` OAuth scope and the PR's diff touches `.github/workflows/` — a deterministic, session-wide precondition distinct from generic `unavailable` (#812; see `skills/worker-preamble/auto-merge.md` step 1.1). `gated-external`: external-author origin — auto-merge intentionally skipped, needs-human-review applied. `unarmed-policy-override`: producing this PR required disabling/bypassing/overriding a committed security or supply-chain control (see `policy_override`) — auto-merge is intentionally never armed regardless of `originating_author_trust`, needs-human-review applied (#1088). `unarmed-gate-narrowing`: this PR narrows a required CI gate rather than fixing the underlying cause (see `gate_narrowing`) — a self-authored allowlist/exception file, a raised severity threshold, `continue-on-error: true`, a deleted gate step, or a narrowed trigger filter; a DIFFERENT risk class from `unarmed-policy-override` (the control stays nominally in place, just weaker for every future PR) — auto-merge is intentionally never armed regardless of `originating_author_trust`, needs-human-review applied (#1139). Null for non-issue-work modes.

policy_override.description: When `auto_merge == "unarmed-policy-override"`, a one-line name of the committed security/supply-chain control that was disabled, bypassed, or overridden while producing this PR — e.g. ".npmrc min-release-age=7" — mirroring the `(policy-override: <control>)` free-text suffix (#1088; see `skills/worker-preamble/SKILL.md` § "Never disable a committed security or supply-chain control" and `skills/worker-preamble/auto-merge.md` step 0.3). Null unless that auto_merge value is set.

gate_narrowing.description: When `auto_merge == "unarmed-gate-narrowing"`, a one-line name of the signal `detect-ci-gate-narrowing.sh` tripped on — e.g. "new allowlist file .github/security/audit-allowlist.json" or "raised --audit-level low<high" — mirroring the `(gate-narrowing: <signal>)` free-text suffix (#1139; see `skills/worker-preamble/auto-merge.md` step 0.34 and `scripts/detect-ci-gate-narrowing.sh`). Null unless that auto_merge value is set.

awaiting_what.description: When `outcome == "awaiting-external"`, a one-line identification of the external job being waited on — e.g. "mobile-e2e run 31859829802" — mirroring the `awaiting-external #<N>: <what>` free-text token (#1390). Must be specific enough that a human reading the end-of-session summary knows exactly which job stalled, and stable enough that a second park naming the same string is recognizable as a re-park on the same job. Null unless that outcome is set.

awaiting_probe.description: When `outcome == "awaiting-external"`, the single read-only command the ORCHESTRATOR will execute verbatim, once per periodic-refresh tick, to learn whether the job has finished — e.g. "gh run view 31859829802 --json status,conclusion" (#1390). Because this string is executed rather than merely read, it is an injection surface: it MUST pass `scripts/validate-awaiting-external-probe.sh` (a read-only allowlist — no chaining, no substitution, no redirection, GET-only `gh api`) both worker-side before it is returned and orchestrator-side before it is ever run. A probe that fails validation is never executed; the park degrades to a `blocked:` hand-back. Null unless that outcome is set.

awaiting_eta.description: Optional. When `outcome == "awaiting-external"`, the worker's rough estimate of how long the external job still needs — e.g. "~40m" — mirroring the `eta <duration>` free-text token (#1390). Advisory only: it feeds the status line and the end-of-session summary, and it is NEVER the bound. The actual bound is `awaiting_external.max_hours` (default 2), anchored at the first park, so an optimistic or absent estimate cannot extend the wait.

checks.description: One-shot snapshot of the PR's check rollup at return time (latest run per check name, per #333) — the structured form of the return-string `checks: …` suffix. NEVER a wait: the worker returns on green|pending|failing alike (#707). Null when no PR is involved.

head_sha.description: For a fix-checks-only `green`/`noop` outcome: the PR's full head commit SHA (`headRefOid`) the worker observed the rollup at — the structured form of the free-text `@<head-SHA>` token (#1211, the deferred half of #1205). Load-bearing for the orchestrator's step-A reconcile: a `green`/`noop` outcome whose `head_sha` doesn't match the PR's live `headRefOid` is treated exactly like a #1205 fabrication-tell trip — classified strictly off a live `gh pr view` spot-check, never off the claim. NOT schema-required (a green/noop outcome without it is still schema-valid, matching the free-text shape's own backward-compatible transition-window handling) — a missing value forces the SAME unconditional live spot-check green/noop already always gets, so omitting it never earns LESS scrutiny than citing it. Null/absent for every other mode/outcome combination.

disposition.description: For `disposition` outcomes from investigate / spike / issue-work mode: how the issue was dispositioned. `fix` — rewrote into a real spec and opened a fixing PR (pr is then set). `needs-human-review` — handed to the human queue; see `summary` for whether the label was actually (re-)applied — a worker that ran the decision-freshness check (#1279, `shipyard:worker-preamble`'s `decision-freshness-check.md`) and found the human already answered this exact question since the last escalation reports `disposition: "needs-human-review"` WITHOUT applying the label (the free-text return's `(decision already recorded, gate not re-applied)` suffix is the signal; the orchestrator's reconcile must NOT independently re-apply `needs-human-review` for that suffix). `auto-close-noise` — closed as non-actionable noise. `duplicate` — closed as a duplicate. `verified` — (issue-work's §6.6 verification disposition, #852) ran the named auditor against a scope-preflight-supplied verification slice, filed any bug issues the auditor found, and dispositioned the issue (labeled and left open for a manual residual, or closed if fully verified) without opening a resolving PR. Null for code-worker modes that shipped a normal PR. (`decomposed` / `designed` were removed by #860 — spike mode's actual return contract (`agents/issue-worker/spike.md` §11) folds both the design-doc-only and sharded-into-sub-issues outcomes into a single `outcome:"shipped"` (`spiked+shipped`), never a distinct `disposition`; spike's only `disposition` value is `needs-human-review`.)

blocked_reason.description: For `blocked` outcomes, the human-readable reason (the text after `blocked:` in the return string). Load-bearing for the orchestrator's reconcile: a reason naming an open `Blocked by #N` is a dependency-wait (no label); anything else is a refuse (needs-human-review). Null unless outcome == "blocked".

blocked_stage.description: Optional stage annotation for a `blocked` outcome (e.g. "branch-setup", "pre-pr-create", "pre-push", "closing-link-verify") mirroring the `blocked #<N> at <stage>:` free-text form. Null when not applicable.

last_push.description: For `reaped` outcomes, the short hash of the last commit the worker pushed before its worktree was reaped (or null / "none" if it never pushed). Mirrors the `(last push: <hash|none>)` suffix so a re-dispatch can tell whether any work survived on the remote.

worktree_path.description: Optional. The absolute path of the git worktree the worker actually ran in, self-reported from its own step-0 cwd fail-fast (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` / `scripts/assert-worktree-cwd.sh`'s `toplevel=` diagnostic) — an absolute path here is correct and expected; this is a distinct field from any repo-relative path a worker names in prose per the #1220 narration convention. Lets the orchestrator's reconcile answer "did this worker operate outside its own worktree?" with a direct string comparison against the `worktreePath` it dispatched this work unit with, instead of inferring it from prose or content archaeology (#1221). Absent on a worker running an older prompt that doesn't populate it — degrades to no signal, exactly as before this field existed; never required. Detection/reporting only — `enforce-worktree-isolation.sh` already blocks the real violation at write time, so a mismatch here is an advisory, never a new enforcement gate.

summary.description: Optional one-line human-readable summary for the orchestrator's end-of-session report. Not consumed by reconcile logic — provenance only.

allOf.$comment: A blocked outcome must carry a reason.
A disposition outcome must name how it dispositioned.
An awaiting-external outcome must name the job AND the probe the orchestrator will run (#1390).
An unarmed-policy-override auto_merge value must name the overridden control (#1088).
An unarmed-gate-narrowing auto_merge value must name the tripped signal (#1139).
